_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for NEE retrospectives (retro/build_nee.py): FPL Group, Inc. (NYSE: FPL), NextEra Energy, Inc. from the 8-K of 2010-05-24 (`company_names`) and NYSE: NEE from 2010-06-23 (`listings`); NEE is the series key and Yahoo's symbol. Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date: a filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR records no time before 2003). The earnings 8-Ks of Q2 2007 to Q3 2013 were accepted before the open (07:30-08:58 ET) on the release day, six of them on a Friday; the 10-Ks came weeks later, so a Q4 print carries its year's actuals (fy_actual) until the 10-K. Every EPS guide of 2007-2013 is a range of 'adjusted earnings', which also excludes the mark-to-market effect of non-qualifying hedges (and, from 2008, other than temporary impairment losses), recurring items: the guides are display only ('guides', the PEP 2008 core rule) and the history is GAAP, except 1999 and 2000 at the company's figures excluding only one-offs. No filing guides revenue or a margin. Generated by a script from row strings of the filings (each checked with retro/tools/verbatim.py); every growth rate, margin, margin change and rule-T value is computed, not typed (retro/README.md, 'NEE').

splits.note: 'In February 2005, FPL Group's board of directors approved a two-for-one stock split of FPL Group's common stock effective March 15, 2005 (2005 stock split).' (NE8); Yahoo's split date is 2005-03-16, the first trading day on the new basis. The FY2004 10-K, published before it, says 'The per share information does not reflect the effect of the 2005 stock split.' (NE7), so per-share figures published before 2005-03-16 are halved and share counts doubled (on_basis); every print, guide and dividend of the range follows it
